steps.action: Public-source recovery pass for historical NOC PRISM/TOBI navigation semantics
details: JC007 cruise processing report states that checked .nav and .cable files are passed to wireout, which dynamically models TOBI position and produces a .veh_nav file; mrgnav_inertia then correlates .veh_nav with imagery headers to calculate each ping position.
JC007 example processing uses mrgnav_inertia with a 200 m umbilical and navfile.veh_nav, and explicitly says cable values are taken from the cable file rather than TOBI header when -t is omitted.
JC024 report states wireout assumes cable drag and viscosity plus sidescan/towed-body effects and a depth value related to cable length, giving an initial TOBI-position estimate.

A historical PRISM processing report explains assumptions including straight cable, cable-value correctness, zero cable at depressor water-entry, an inertial navigation algorithm, a nominal 200 m umbilical plus a cruise/platform GPS-to-water-entry offset. These are generic historical semantics and are not yet CD169-specific configuration.

JR63 report independently warns that PRISM wireout navigation can behave poorly in turns and may push the vehicle outward, making V2 turn/outlier diagnostics scientifically relevant rather than removable noise.
